fixed.problem: Blocking 2 (W15-24 regression): the fixer's CONNECTORS list took any connector (on, in, for, with, from, at, by, to, ...) after a command with no written argument as 'its arguments are described'. So commands that the base ran silently stopped being tried, with no not-tried line in their place. That covered tools that take no argument ('Running node hello.js in a terminal / from the command line prints ...', 'node greet.js to print a greeting', '... at the prompt') and bare runs said in words ('node app.js by itself exits with code 1', 'node wc.js on its own ...').
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/try-plan.test.ts 'w15-review, wave 15' > 'W15-24: a command said with where or how it runs, not what it is given, is tried as before', 'W15-24: a tool that takes no argument is tried from a sentence that says where it runs; a bare run said in words expects its error', 'W15-24: a tool whose input is only described, and that no written command runs, is told as not tried, never silently left out'
fixed.how: try-plan.ts: words that say where or how a command runs (in, from, at, to, by, into, onto, through, about, over, alone) are back in GOES_ON. They end the command as written, as on the base. Only INTRODUCES_INPUT words (on, with, for, against, using, given, passing) can mark a command `described`, and only when describesInput finds the name of an input (INPUT_NOUN: file, path, text, input, argument, name, folder, csv, flag, ...) within the next six words, before a word that goes on. So 'on its own', 'on the command line' and 'with Node 22' end the command, and 'with no arguments' stays a bare run, whose own sentence or bareRunFails sets expectsError. planTries collects described scripts (describedOnly). For each one that no written command runs, it adds 'wc.js was not tried: an acceptance criterion says in words what it is given, not the command to run'. The old 'reads its command line, but neither the brief nor a README says how to run it', which was untrue there, is skipped for such a script. Live check 2's wc.js case is unchanged: it tries only 'node wc.js <file>' and has no notTried line. ADR 0110's amendment point 1 and runtime.md are rewritten to match.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Bench (walked, steps 09-10 under /tmp/frbench/fixup-w15-review/steps): create coder task 'Write the greeting tool in hello.js' with the criterion 'Running node hello.js from the command line prints a greeting', and coder task 'Write the word counter in wc.js' with the criterion "node wc.js on a file containing 'a b c' prints 3". Start, then open each drawer's 'See what was checked'. hello.js should read 'node hello.js: worked / ran node hello.js (from an acceptance criterion) ...' (on the fixer's head it was not tried at all). wc.js should read 'wc.js was not tried: an acceptance criterion says in words what it is given, not the command to run'. Live check 3 (step S6, unchanged): brief 'A command line tool that counts the words in a file. Usage: node wc.js <file>.', then Approve and start. Expect Done · Reviewed and tried after one run, with only 'node wc.js <file>: worked' tried and no 'Sent back: Tried node wc.js' line.

fixed.problem: Blocking 1 (W15-25 regression): retryConstraints dropped a whole finding from a research retry brief when its description or its required action named a host the site rule refuses, or anything that looks like a host ('socket.io'). Under an 'only' rule, the reviewer's two findings ('figures for vercel.com ... come from memory' -> 'Remove those figures ...'; 'socket.io is required' -> 'Drop socket.io ...') both vanished, and the retry got no findings at all. That breaks design §4.6.
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/research-web.test.ts 'w15-review, wave 15' > 'W15-25: under a site rule every finding reaches the retry brief; a host in a finding's words or an action that reads no page is no reason to drop it' (before: no 'Critic findings to resolve' in the brief the model received). The extended 'W15-25: after Go ahead without, the next brief holds no order to read a page the site rule refuses' also fails before (the finding was dropped, not kept with its order replaced).
fixed.how: executor.ts: every non-note finding is an order again. Only a required action for which asksForRefusedPage holds is replaced by REFUSED_PAGE_ACTION ('The page this asks for is one the project's rule refuses: do not read it; meet the finding from what the rule allows, or say in the report what the rule kept out.'). The finding's description is kept as is. asksForRefusedPage reads the required action clause by clause. It looks for an order to read in an order's place (clause start, or after and/then/or/to/also/first/please/must/should/now/comma): fetch, read, open, visit, browse, load, retrieve, consult, download, access, scrape, crawl, cite, quote, look up, go to, web_fetch. It also takes 'check/verify/confirm/compare … against/on/at/with' and 'source/take/get/pull/copy/use … from'. The order counts only when a host the rule refuses follows it in the same clause. A host in the description, a host in an action that removes, marks or fixes something, and the same words used as nouns ('the quote from …', 'the access dates for …') change nothing. WEB_RULE_WINS_LINE follows once whenever the rule refuses anything and findings are listed. ADR 0107's amendment point 2 and runtime.md are rewritten to match.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Live check 3 (step S4, extended): under web_access {mode:'only', only:['10.1.2.3']}, add a researcher task naming an MDN page and Start. If the critic sends it back, press Go ahead without or let the retry run. In the model-call log, the next researcher brief should list every open finding under 'Critic findings to resolve'. A finding whose action asked to fetch a developer.mozilla.org page should read '<description> -> The page this asks for is one the project's rule refuses: ...', and the brief should not contain 'Fetch https://developer.mozilla.org'. A finding that asks to remove or mark figures should keep its own action. 'The project's rule on which websites research may read comes before any finding ...' should appear once.

INPUT_NOUN is a word list: an odd sentence such as 'node wc.js for a quick word count prints ...' reads 'word' as a described input, and the command is told as not tried instead of run bare. It is rare, and it is said in See what was checked, never silent.
